case_name: Ram Swarup and Others v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

14 July 1993
Cr.A. Nos. 406-07 of 1990 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 7 February 1990 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Cr. No. 30-DB of 1988)
The Judgment was delivered by: N. P. SINGH, J.
1.  Two appeals have been filed against the same judgment. Criminal Appeal No. 406 of 1990 has been filed on behalf of Ram Swarup, Pala Ram and Mela Ram; whereas Criminal Appeal No. 407 has been filed on behalf of Hari Ram, Brijlal and Prem. All the six accused persons had been put on trial for causing the death of Biru Ram and injuries on Ranjit Ram (PW 4), Dharampal (PW 5), Ajmer Singh (PW 10), Joginder Singh (PW 11), Smt Phoola Devi

statutes.act: Read With Section 149 Of The Indian Penal Code
Read With Section 149 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: Two appeals have been filed against the same judgment.
The case is about a dispute between two families over a wall and its construction.
The appellants were accused of causing the death of Biru Ram and injuries on others.
The prosecution party had suffered 20 injuries, while the accused party had suffered fewer injuries.
The trial court and High Court had referred to the different injuries found on the person of the appellants and Smt Satya Devi (DW 1).
The nature and number of injuries on the persons of complainant party suggest that the accused were the aggressors.
issues: Whether the prosecution party or the accused party was the aggressor.
Whether the appellants had any common intention to cause the death of Biru Ram.
petitioner_arguments: The real onus is on the prosecution party to prove its case, including the manner of occurrence beyond all reasonable doubts; the accused has only to raise a doubt in the mind of the court or to satisfy the court that the defence version disclosed by the accused was a probable version of the occurrence.
respondent_arguments: The number of injuries on the persons of complainant party suggest that the accused were the aggressors.
court_reasoning: The question cannot be determined on basis of the number of injuries found on the side of the complainant or the accused person.
All the evidence adduced on behalf of the parties and relevant circumstances have to be taken into consideration.
In such cases it cannot be urged that there are two parallel versions of the occurrence before the court.
holding: The conviction and sentence, under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, of the appellants, Hari Ram, Brijlal, Ram Swarup, Pala Ram and Mela Ram are set aside.
Their conviction and sentence under Section 326 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 by the trial Court, which have been affirmed by the High Court are upheld.
